title_zh: 水龙头与离职信：一条路怎样才算真的开着
title_en: The Tap and the Resignation Letter: What Makes a Way Out Real?
deck_zh: 十四个人的水厂也能握住一千户的命脉；合同上可以辞职，也未必走得开。SAE从泉坳与青窑的虚构故事，说明关口、供给职责和人不可被买走的去向。
deck_en: A tiny water company can hold a village's lifeline, and a right to resign can coexist with practical captivity. Two fictional towns reveal what supply duties and genuine freedom to leave require.
body_zh: ## 小公司，也可能守着很深的关口
先到论文虚构的泉坳。上坳约四百户，下坳约六百户，唯一的自来水公司只有十四名员工。公司铺了管，还给小学免费接水。后来它以泉眼减产、设备更新为由涨价六成，冬天对二十三户欠费人家停水，其中两户有卧床老人。公司说：我们只是不再供自己的水。
它不一定在说谎，问题是这句话没有把关系说完。SAE把别人维持生活或展开自己时实际绕不过去的位置，叫作关口。关口有广度，也有深度：四万家卖家要经过的平台很宽；一千户人家唯一可负担的水源很深。规模小，不等于权力浅。认出关口也不等于判公司有罪：它确实带来了更方便的供水，涨价也可能有真实成本。要问的是，它在这个位置上做了什么。
名义上的替代不算现成的路。泉坳能叫运水车，但每吨贵四倍；能打井，但上坳申请审了五个月；下坳的旧井则早被填平。价格能吸引竞争者，是重要的市场机制，可竞争者得来得及进来。停水的那个冬天，价格信号没有替人送来水。
## 停供不是一种事，要把前史带进来
SAE不从需要直接推出任何人都必须永远供应。没有承诺、没有被制度或稳定关系确认为可主张的供给位置、也没有先堵掉别人的路，停止自己的供给，不因此就是侵犯。公司仍须说明自己的安排，但不能仅凭别人依赖它，就无限征用它的资源。
第二种情形是已经承担的供给。下坳有铺管与统一供水协议；上坳没签同一份协议，却接管、付费五年，公司也按一套规则收费和处理欠费。州的取水许可还写着供应两村。这不是陌生人临时施舍：公司与制度一直把住户当作可以主张供水的位置。撤回要核对已经成立的承诺与职责，不能假装关系从未发生。
第三种情形更明确：先排他性封路，使人依赖，再撤回。下坳原有三口出水的公井，公司按协议取得井址并填井，五年后停水。它不是只拿走自己的新增供给，还握着自己关掉的旧路。上坳的井却是陆续干涸，原因未查明，不能算到公司头上；新井审批拖延，也要问州的审批位置。唯一供给与主动独占，不是一回事。
三种读法不是互斥的盒子。下坳既有供水承诺，也有填井的前史，要分别核账。恢复被关闭的自维通路，是停止压缩别人，不是额外施恩。可以重开井，也可以另建同样可用、有保障的路；水质与接续办法仍须查清，不能一句重开就算完。
下坳约六成村民当年赞成协议，这个反对意见有分量：公司铺了管、两年半价，旧井也确有一次细菌超标。但交换的好处不能抵销封路。可撤回的授权，与把撤回也封死的让渡，结构不同；协议是否留下修订退出通道，材料没有写。其余四成也不能被编成全体反对者。村委会约束未表示赞成者的权限，本身另受检查。
## 可以追水费，不能拿维持生命的水催债
SAE的底线不是给所有商品宣布一个正确价格。水是资源，生命与身体才是要保护的基础维度；经由控制资源关闭这些维度，才触到基础权利。因此应问某项作用把谁挡在维持生命的条件之外，而不是只问水在不在一张清单上。清单与用量标准可以由具体制度制定，不能取代对实际人家的判断。
论文又设想山洪冲坏净水站，公司三天修好，一个月收三倍价。三倍这个数字不自动证明掠夺：抢修成本未量化。它若没有导致断供，也没有逼人做别的事，仍是交换条件。可它若导致住户失去维持生命的水，那一部分就不能靠成本理由消掉。
这里还有一道区分。拿供水要求付已经认可的水费，是要求履约；拿供水逼人卖地、不上访、照指定方向投票，是替人决定本来属于他的事。前者目标可以正当，后者已经越过交换。但正当目标也不能让所有手段正当：在已经承诺、确认为供给位置或先封路的关系中，维持喝水、做饭、基本清洁的那份水，不能被拿作催债杠杆。交得起却不交，与确实交不起，影响债怎样追，不改变这一底线。新增六成的价格是否已被两村认可，还要另核。
反对者问：那谁付账，公司是慈善机构吗？不是。欠款没有取消，水也不必免费；禁止的是以切断生命条件追债，不是让经营成本消失。由此要把另一方叫进来：管理这个地方的制度或政府。
## 保障供水，不等于把十四个人绑在水厂
生命基底处没有可负担替代的供给位置，不只是经营自己的资产，也在承接公共保障的执行。它的职责有两个来路：住户被制度、共同体有效承认和真实执行力量共同支持的供给权利，反过来约束供给者；管理者把公共供水交给这个位置，也使它承担执行职责。泉坳的日常收费规则、长期使用关系和限定用途的取水许可，提供了这些根据。不是住户先服从公司，才换到一份权利。
所以要分工：供给位置负责供给，管理者负责创造供得下去的条件，包括付不起者怎样不断水、价格由谁审、原经营者撤出时谁接续。现有法律只管五千户以上供水者，泉坳约一千户，委员会没有水价权限；这说明制度有待回答的空档，不说明底线被取消，也不证明所有其他救济都不存在。
职责束缚位置，不把员工投资人终身绑住。退出可以有效，但退出有效不等于一纸六个月通知就完成接续：留下管网，也不能代替实际可用的接续安排。管理者须接住过渡，不能拿自己的缺位变成某个人无限续供的义务。要保住的是水，不是保证这家公司永远不倒；经营者可以替换，已经发生的不当停供也不被后来的退出洗掉。
## 几条合同合起来，可能把门一层层关上
再到虚构的青窑镇。青窑瓷业雇着约七成适龄劳动人口，工资高同行一成，免费办学徒班，还修了出镇的路。它拥有镇上四成住房，宿舍离职后三十天腾退；工资两成是仅在公司商店食堂使用的窑券，商店价格比苹果城高约一成五；预支未还，离职须公司同意；离职须提前三个月通知；离职后两年，全州不得做瓷业，违约赔十二个月工资。
期限、还款、搬家，不能一概等同囚禁，也不能先宣布每条都没问题。关键是同一个人的实际组合。老窑工做了三十一年，想与同事另开窑坊：欠四个月预支时，公司不同意；借亲戚的钱还清，又被竞业条款拦住；后来榆钱长期合伙出资，付六个月工资换公司书面放弃那条限制，他才走成。宿舍与窑券在他这次退出中实际起了多大作用，材料没写，不能补成因果；但审查一般职工能否离开时，它们必须与其他条件一起算。
工资高、预支救急、宿舍真实有用，都照记。给予不能抵销封路，封路也不把给予变假。入职签字证明当时接受条款，不证明组合后仍有可负担的拒绝、撤回或复核通道。纸上可以辞职，与生计上走得开，是两回事。
## 你的去向，不是培养你的人所有的东西
对离职后禁去向，SAE的立场更明确：竞业禁止拿走人选择发展方向的权利，原则上不应允许。能否把窑坊办成，当然取决于客户、本钱和别人的选择；但可以尝试往那里走，不该事先由原雇主划掉。只管一个行业、一个地区、两年，改变的是侵入的范围，不是性质；签字或补偿也不能把禁止变成自由选择。保护商业秘密是护住自己的权利，不是禁止别人往某个人生方向走。
这也适用于后来老窑工自己的窑坊：到第二十五年，它雇了二十二人，包括九名青窑裁员者，却规定学徒满师两年不得在本镇开窑。范围更窄，仍把一块方向预先写成不可选。判的是条款，不是把曾经受限、后来设限的人定性为坏人。为保护第三人权利或公共追问而严格限住某一种越界行为的安排，则不是为雇主留人挡竞争的竞业禁止；它必须说明护谁、为何必要、范围多宽，并保留退出与复核。
真正额外、可以拒绝的条件给付不同。例如不在本镇开窑两年，可以领一笔额外的钱；仍可去开窑，只是不领。这不是买走方向，而是一个人仍握着方向，自己取舍。要过三关：后果只是停发额外给付，不是罚款禁令；钱不是已挣工资、递延报酬或追缴已付款；与债务住房等合看，拒绝不会等于活不下去。只说自愿，只说不追回，都还不够。
乔氏基金会后来为九百名被裁职工提供三年生活费，约原工资九成，要进入指定设计园、选三条培训路，并三年不得为别的瓷企工作。退出停发、不追已付；但退出后禁令是否仍在，文件没写。若不领钱也不许去，就是禁止；若仅停发，仍须核给付是否额外、基础生活是否有着落。不能替基金会补一个好答案，也不能直接定罪。
还须分清对象：人的分叉权，不能直接套在公司之间。投资协议约定窑坊三年不接其他投资人的钱，应按关口与制衡另审，不等同于禁止一个人离职后的去向。
为什么这么看重退出？不是因为人人都该辞职创业，而是人必须保有离开、换关系、另开路径的现实可能。老窑工获资助后确实开出了新路，但两位同事没有同样出资而留下，原因未全记载。一位被挑中的能工巧匠走成，不证明普通人的路也通。SAE要守的是每个人不被既有安排穷尽的空间，也守住新合作与新制度能够出现的前提：留下是自己的选择，不是门外还有一道门。
body_en: ## A small business can hold a very deep chokepoint

Imagine a water company with fourteen employees serving two villages. It builds the network, connects the schools free of charge, and makes daily life easier. Years later, citing a shrinking spring and equipment costs, it raises prices by 60 percent. In winter, it disconnects twenty-three households, including two with bedridden older residents. Its defense sounds straightforward: we are merely withdrawing our own supply.

Springhollow is fictional, as are its laws and the later Bluekiln examples. The purpose is to test a principle, not to report misconduct by real companies. SAE's principle starts with a chokepoint: a position that others cannot practically bypass when sustaining their lives or pursuing their development. Breadth asks how many must pass through it. Depth asks what is at stake when they cannot. A marketplace serving thousands of sellers has breadth; a tiny supplier controlling affordable drinking water has depth. Size alone measures neither responsibility nor wrongdoing.

A supposed alternative must be usable. In Springhollow, delivered water costs four times as much, permission for a new well has been pending for five months, and another village's wells have been filled in. Higher prices can attract entrants, but only if entry is possible soon enough. That winter, a price signal does not deliver water. Recognizing the chokepoint still does not establish that the price rise is unjustified: the company may face genuine costs, and its original contribution remains real.
## Three different histories behind the same disconnection

SAE does not turn someone's need into an unlimited claim on any available supplier. Where there was no promise, no established claim-bearing supply arrangement, and no prior obstruction of alternatives, withdrawing one's own contribution is not, simply for that reason, an infringement. An organization must still explain its decisions, but dependence alone does not conscript its resources forever.

An established supply relationship is different. Lower Hollow has an agreement for pipes and unified supply. Upper Hollow has no equivalent agreement, but households have connected, paid for five years, and been billed under the company's continuing rules. A public extraction permit specifies supply to both villages. These arrangements treat residents as customers with claims, not occasional recipients of a gift. Withdrawal must therefore be assessed against responsibilities already undertaken or institutionally recognized.

A third history is more serious: first close someone's route to maintaining themselves, make them dependent, then withdraw. Lower Hollow had three functioning public wells. Under the agreement, the company acquired their sites and filled them in. Five years later it disconnects households. It is still holding shut a route that its own actions removed. Upper Hollow's wells dried up for an undetermined reason; the evidence does not attribute that to the company. Nor is the company automatically responsible for the state's delayed well permit. Being the only supplier is not identical to having actively monopolized supply.

These are overlapping questions, not exclusive boxes. Lower Hollow's supply commitment and the destruction of its wells each require an account. Ending an obstruction is not bestowing a new favor: it is stopping a continuing compression of someone else's possibilities. Reopening wells, creating an equally usable alternative, or securing replacement supply could address it. Water quality and implementation still need examination.

About 60 percent of Lower Hollow's assembly approved the agreement. That matters: pipes, two years of half-price water, and concern after one contaminated sample were genuine considerations. But consent does not erase the structure of what happened. Delegating authority while retaining revision and withdrawal is different from surrendering the means to withdraw. The record does not establish every exit provision or explain how the remaining residents voted. Neither wholesale invalidation of the agreement nor invented unanimous opposition follows.
## Collect the debt without using life as collateral

Why protect water? SAE does not begin with an eternal list of commodities or a morally correct price. Water is a resource; life and bodily integrity are the foundational dimensions. Controlling a resource can violate those dimensions when it closes their actual means of maintenance. Concrete institutions can specify protected quantities and services, but the central question remains whose life a particular action obstructs.

Consider the paper's further hypothetical: a flood damages the treatment plant, repairs take three days, and the company charges triple for one month. That multiplier does not by itself prove exploitation; repair costs are unspecified. A price for the supplied thing remains an exchange condition. Using water to demand that a family sell land, abandon a petition, or vote a certain way instead substitutes the supplier's judgment for the family's own. Demanding payment of an acknowledged bill is not the same kind of demand. Whether residents accepted the additional 60 percent is a separate, unresolved question.

Yet a legitimate objective does not license every means. Within a relationship involving prior obstruction, promise, or recognized supply, the water necessary to sustain life must be removed from the machinery of debt collection. Whether a household cannot pay or refuses despite being able affects recovery of the debt; it does not make vital water available as leverage. The debt can remain payable while disconnection is ruled out as its enforcement tool.

Who pays, then? This objection correctly identifies a cost; it does not justify ignoring the boundary. The company is not a charity. Protection must bring the responsible public institution into the account, rather than quietly assigning an unlimited bill to the supplier.
## Secure the supply, not the company's immortality

An irreplaceable provider at the foundation of life is doing more than managing an investment. It occupies a position through which a wider institution delivers part of its public guarantee. SAE identifies two sources of duty. Residents' recognized supply claims constrain the provider, supported by institutional incorporation, effective community recognition, and real enforcing power. Separately, the governing institution assigns or incorporates this supply function. In Springhollow, continuing billing, established use, and the permit's public purpose supply the relevant grounds. Residents do not earn rights by first submitting to corporate authority.

The division of responsibility matters. The supply position must deliver; the governing institution must create conditions that make delivery sustainable, including arrangements for those unable to pay, price scrutiny, and replacement when an operator leaves. The fictional utility law covers only suppliers serving more than five thousand households, leaving Springhollow's roughly one thousand outside the commission's price jurisdiction. That gap does not cancel the underlying responsibility. It also does not prove that no other remedy exists.

Duties attach to a position, not a lifetime of personal service. Investors and workers are not permanently bound to the plant. But an effective exit requires a transition process; announcing six months' notice and leaving pipes behind does not make them produce water without a spring or treatment facility. Public failure to organize succession must not become one person's indefinite obligation. Secure water, not the perpetual survival of this particular firm. The operator may change or fail, while past wrongful disconnections remain accountable.
## A contract can close doors one after another

In fictional Bluekiln, a porcelain company employs about 70 percent of working-age labor. Its wages exceed the state industry average by 10 percent; it trains apprentices without tuition and has built a road. It also owns 40 percent of local housing, requires departure from its dormitories within thirty days of resignation, and pays 20 percent of wages in vouchers usable only at its shop and canteen. The shop charges about 15 percent more than Apple City. Outstanding advances require company permission to leave; resignation requires three months' notice; a two-year statewide non-compete threatens twelve months' wages in damages.

A potter with thirty-one years' experience wants to open a workshop with colleagues. With four months of advances outstanding, permission is denied. Relatives lend him repayment money, but the non-compete still stops him. Eventually Elmseed Long-Term Partners funds a settlement of six months' wages, and the company waives the restriction in writing. Only then does he leave.

Repayment, notice, and moving requirements are not automatically captivity. Nor should each be assumed harmless in isolation. Examine the same person's combined circumstances against the same boundary: can they refuse, withdraw from continuing attachment, or obtain meaningful review? Housing and vouchers belong in that inquiry, although the story does not establish their exact causal role in this potter's departure. A signature establishes acceptance, not a practically affordable exit. Higher wages and useful advances remain benefits; they neither offset obstruction nor become fictitious because obstruction exists.
## A person's next direction is not the employer's property

On post-employment non-competes, SAE takes an affirmative position: they remove a person's choice of developmental direction and should in principle not be allowed. Succeeding as a potter depends on customers, finance, and other people's decisions; no one owes the departing worker commercial success. But permission to try that direction is a different matter. A prohibition backed by damages or an injunction deletes a direction before the attempt can begin. Narrow territory or duration reduces its reach, not its nature. Signature and compensation do not restore the removed choice.

The same standard applies to the former employee's own workshop. By year twenty-five it employs twenty-two people, including nine workers laid off by Bluekiln, but its apprentice contract prohibits opening a kiln in town for two years after qualification. Narrower, yet still a prohibition on direction. This judges a clause, not the moral character of someone who has occupied both sides of such a relationship.

Protecting confidential formulas or customer information is different from banning a life direction. So are narrowly justified restrictions on a particular exercise that would violate third parties' rights or obstruct public accountability. Those arrangements must identify whom they protect, why less restriction is insufficient, and what review remains available. Merely invoking protection cannot disguise a prohibition serving the employer's own interest in deterring competition. Training costs can be addressed through arrangements whose exit burdens are separately examined; training does not confer ownership of the trainee's future.

A genuinely additional, rejectable payment also differs. Suppose someone remains free to open a kiln but can receive extra money by choosing not to do so locally for two years. Three tests must hold together: refusal stops only that additional payment, rather than triggering prohibition or punishment; the money is not earned wages, deferred compensation, or previously paid funds reclaimed; and, considering dependence and other obligations, refusing does not mean being unable to survive. Formal optionality alone is insufficient.

The later Qiao Foundation program illustrates an unresolved boundary. After nine hundred layoffs, it offers three years of living support, about 90 percent of former wages, tied to a designated design park, three training tracks, and no work for other porcelain firms for three years. Departing stops payments without reclaiming past support. The plan does not say whether the work restriction survives departure. If it does, it is a prohibition; if not, the other payment tests still need checking. The missing answer must not be invented in either direction.

The right to choose a developmental direction belongs to people. A workshop's three-year agreement not to accept another investor is not automatically a human non-compete. Interorganizational exclusivity instead requires its own examination of chokepoints and checks.

Real exit does more than rescue today's dissatisfied worker. It keeps new relationships and alternatives possible. The funded potter genuinely creates a new workshop, but that success does not establish affordable departure for an ordinary worker. Two colleagues without the same funding stay; their full reasons are not recorded. SAE does not demand that everybody leave. It demands a social arrangement in which staying can remain a choice, and a fresh route need not depend on a benefactor paying to unlock the final door.
takeaway_zh: 关口必须留下真实可用的自维与退出通路，基础生活不能用来催服从，人的离职后去向也不能被合同买断。
takeaway_en: Chokepoints must preserve usable routes to self-maintenance and exit: vital supply cannot compel obedience, and a contract cannot purchase a person's future direction.
editorial_notes: 本篇依据源论文第二篇；泉坳、青窑及法律条款均明确为虚构论证设例，未改写为现实史实。
保留供给退出三分法、承认性载入、下坳填井与上坳原因未明的差别，以及唯一基础供给职责的受供给者/管理者两处来源。
竞业禁止按原论文明确立场重写：原则上不容许离职后禁去向，签字、补偿、缩窄范围不改变性质；与条件给付三判据、保护第三人和保密安排区分。
保留乔氏计划退出后禁令未明、老窑工宿舍窑券作用未明、两同事留下原因未全等事实限度；案例链接仅作延伸，不认定与设例完全同构。
为面向普通读者，省去命题编号与波兰尼、汤普森、赫希曼二手文献对照，完整保留本篇主要规范论证和具体反对意见。英文为独立结构重写。
